evidence: app/package.json:6-16 — react-router/@react-router/* pinned at 8.5.1, the current stable release (verified via npm and reactrouter.com/changelog); no preview/canary channels
app/react-router.config.ts:3-5 — config is only `{ ssr: true }`, no future flags, no unstable_* options
app/app/routes/not-found.tsx:1 — `data()` utility, stable since v7 (and 6.24-era router releases)
app/app/root.tsx:1,11 — `Layout` export plus Links/Meta/Outlet/Scripts/ScrollRestoration, the standard stable root convention
reach.rationale: The app reaches for zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs; every framework API in use has been stable since v6.4–v7, far longer than six months. It runs the newest stable major (v8, June 2026) but uses none of v8's new features, and v8 itself adopted all previously-flagged behavior as default.

evidence: app/app/routes.ts:1-12 — small explicit route config using only `index`/`route`, no unstable route config extensions
app/build/server/index.js:1309 — the only `unstable_*` strings anywhere under app/ are in framework-generated build output, not source
containment.rationale: There is nothing to contain: no experimental APIs in source, and the framework-internal future-flag defaults only appear in generated build artifacts.

evidence: app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:2 — imports are `data, Link, useSearchParams`, all stable equivalents of what the spec needs
app/package.json:11 — `isbot ^5`, a stable third-party library, no beta dependencies
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, so nothing is unjustified; the app solves the spec entirely with long-stable primitives.

findings.issue: The production build output (build/server, build/client) is committed under app/ rather than gitignored, and it embeds framework-internal future-flag defaults (`unstable_apiOnly` etc. at build/server/index.js:1309-1399), which can mislead audits and bloat diffs
findings.suggestion: Add `build/` to .gitignore and rebuild from source in CI; judge source files only for experimental-API analysis

findings.issue: Exact pin `8.5.1` is a same-day patch release, so the lockfile silently freezes on a brand-new build rather than a proven one
findings.suggestion: Keep the exact pin (it is fine for reproducibility) but bump deliberately after a patch has soaked, e.g. track 8.5.x via lockfile updates

summary: This is an unambiguously conservative codebase: it targets the current stable React Router (v8.5.1) and uses only APIs that have been stable since v6.4–v7, with no future flags, unstable names, RSC, middleware, or view transitions anywhere in source. There is no experimental risk to manage; the only notes are hygiene (committed build artifacts) and the freshness of the exact patch pin, neither of which affect runtime behavior.
